findings.reason: The protected source already expresses the optimal earliest-prefix method clearly. The inert candidate makes the material style correction required by this campaign, replacing the forbidden generic locals index and value with the conventional scan variables i and x while preserving the recurrence and contract exactly.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 325 and its Python maxSubArrayLen surface. The Reference preserves contiguous-subarray semantics, the maximum-length result and zero fallback, both explained source examples, and all three signed-value constraints.

The immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064386001 and structurally aligns with the protected app-local source apart from the required class wrapper and legacy List annotation. The candidate preserves the same helper, prefix state, lookup order, and earliest-occurrence rule, changing only local scan names.

The legal alternating zero-sum tiers use 32, 128, and 512 elements, span 16x, and expose repeated matching intervals. The candidate passes all nine executions at +0.01 relative growth and 0.98x; a correct O(n^2) start/end enumeration passes all three benchmark outputs but fails only scaling at +1.17 and 142.38x.

The candidate-targeted Approach exactly derives subarray sums as prefix differences, explains the seeded empty prefix and earliest-occurrence invariant, proves completeness and maximality, and states expected O(n) time with O(n) space.
The hash-bound authenticated Premium Reference remains source-fidelity verified, including both source examples and their explanations in order and all three constraints.

coverage: Both authenticated source examples appear first, in source order, with their exact arrays, targets, and longest lengths.
The invented no-match row is now a trial rather than a source sample, and every formerly hidden whole-array, repeated-prefix, and singleton case is visible.

A one-element trial covers the minimum length; independent verification covers the 200,000-element maximum, and visible trials use element bounds -10,000 and 10,000 plus target bounds -1,000,000,000 and 1,000,000,000.
No-match, singleton, whole-array, interior, negative-target, zero-target, all-zero, and alternating-sign cases exercise every return mode and the seeded empty-prefix behavior.
Repeated equal prefix sums verify that the earliest index must be retained to maximize length; negative values demonstrate why a sliding window is invalid.

A quadratic start/end oracle verified all 11 authored results and all three benchmark results; the candidate also matched it on 214,830 exhaustive array-target pairs with lengths one through six, values from {-2, -1, 0, 1, 2}, and targets -5 through 5.
All 11 correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 32-, 128-, and 512-element alternating zero-sum workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
